```{r}
#| label: setup
# Reads the outputs saved by Take-home_Ex03.qmd, so every number and chart here matches the technical report.
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, leaflet, scales, tidyverse)

rds <- function(name) read_rds(file.path("data/rds", paste0(name, ".rds")))
stations <- rds("stations")
proposed <- rds("proposed")
planning_areas <- rds("planning_areas")
subzones <- rds("subzones")
homes <- rds("homes")
workplaces <- rds("workplaces")
origins <- rds("origins")
code_lookup <- rds("code_lookup")
scenario_results <- rds("scenario_results")
model_fits <- rds("model_fits")
home_access <- rds("home_access")
station_hourly <- rds("station_hourly")
dist_mat <- rds("dist_mat")

fmt_num <- function(x, digits = 0) label_comma(accuracy = 10^-digits)(x)
fmt_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) label_percent(accuracy = 10^-digits)(x)

blue <- "#2a78d6"
aqua <- "#1baf7a"
orange <- "#eb6834"
red <- "#e34948"
grey <- "#898781"
ink <- "#0b0b0b"
ink_secondary <- "#52514e"
land <- "#f0efec"
blue_ramp <- c("#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b")

theme_es <- function(base_size = 18) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      axis.text = element_text(color = ink_secondary),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e1e0d9", linewidth = 0.3),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(color = ink, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "bottom",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", color = NA)
    )
}

map_base <- function() {
  tm_shape(planning_areas) +
    tm_polygons(fill = land, col = "#d9d8d0", lwd = 0.4)
}
map_legend <- function(title) {
  tm_legend(title = title, position = tm_pos_out("right", "center"), frame = FALSE)
}
map_finish <- function() {
  tm_scalebar(position = c("right", "bottom"), breaks = c(0, 5, 10), text.size = 0.6) +
    tm_layout(frame = FALSE, inner.margins = c(0.02, 0.02, 0.02, 0.02), bg.color = "#fcfcfb", outer.bg.color = "#fcfcfb")
}

# Upgraded interchanges are labelled with their proposed-station names, which the station layer lacks
host_names <- proposed |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(proposed_type == "upgraded_interchange") |>
  transmute(station_id = host_station, host_label = str_c(station_name, " (", station_id, ")"))
label_of <- stations |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(host_names, by = "station_id") |>
  transmute(station_id, label = coalesce(host_label, station_label)) |>
  deframe()

baseline <- stations |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(in_baseline)
observed <- baseline$avg_weekday_entries
quiet_threshold <- quantile(observed[!baseline$is_lrt], 0.10)

model_labels <- c(
  M0 = "Distance only",
  M1 = "+ station features",
  M2 = "+ workplace floor area",
  M3 = "+ activity"
)
best_model <- model_fits$best_model
best_fit <- model_fits$fits[[best_model]]
wape <- function(obs, pred) sum(abs(obs - pred)) / sum(obs)
model_wape <- tibble(
  model = names(model_fits$cv_predictions),
  in_sample = map_dbl(model, \(m) wape(observed, model_fits$fits[[m]]$fitted)),
  cv_wape = map_dbl(model, \(m) wape(observed, model_fits$cv_predictions[[m]]))
)
best_wape <- model_wape$cv_wape[model_wape$model == best_model]
distance_wape <- model_wape$cv_wape[model_wape$model == "M0"]

both <- scenario_results |>
  filter(scenario == "both") |>
  mutate(label = label_of[station_id])
existing_run <- scenario_results |>
  filter(scenario == "existing")

new_stations <- both |>
  filter(station_type == "new_alternative") |>
  mutate(quiet = predicted < quiet_threshold)
new_share <- sum(new_stations$predicted) / sum(both$predicted)
top_new <- new_stations |> slice_max(predicted, n = 3)
quiet_new <- new_stations |> filter(quiet) |> arrange(predicted)

station_change <- existing_run |>
  select(station_id, existing = predicted) |>
  inner_join(both |> select(station_id, label, upgraded_by, both = predicted), by = "station_id") |>
  mutate(change = both - existing, change_pct = change / existing)
losers <- station_change |> slice_min(change, n = 3)
interchange_change <- station_change |> filter(!is.na(upgraded_by))
hougang <- interchange_change |> filter(station_id == "NE14")

peak_share <- station_hourly |>
  filter(DAY_TYPE == "WEEKDAY") |>
  group_by(station_id) |>
  summarise(
    peak_share = max(avg_entries) / sum(avg_entries),
    peak_hour = TIME_PER_HOUR[which.max(avg_entries)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
hougang_peak <- peak_share |> filter(station_id == "NE14")

coverage_800 <- function(distance) sum(home_access$home_m2[distance <= 800]) / sum(home_access$home_m2)
cov_before <- coverage_800(home_access$before_m)
cov_after <- coverage_800(home_access$after_m)
gainers <- sum(home_access$saving_m > 0)
far_after <- home_access |>
  group_by(subzone) |>
  summarise(beyond_ha = sum(home_m2[after_m > 800]) / 1e4, .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(beyond_ha, n = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: model-rerun
# Re-applies the report's fitted model, for the two report charts whose inputs were not saved:
# the interchange sensitivity run and the subzone catchment map.
scenario_lines <- list(existing = character(0), both = c("JRL", "CRL"))

scenario_destinations <- function(scenario, uplift = TRUE) {
  added <- scenario_lines[[scenario]]
  stations |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(in_baseline | (station_type == "new_alternative" & line %in% added)) |>
    mutate(n_lines = n_lines_base + as.integer(uplift & !is.na(upgrade_line) & upgrade_line %in% added))
}

theta <- best_fit$theta
log_attraction <- function(dest) {
  if (!"gamma_lines" %in% names(theta)) return(rep(0, nrow(dest)))
  theta[["gamma_lines"]] * log(dest$n_lines) +
    theta[["gamma_bus"]] * log1p(dest[[model_fits$bus_col]]) +
    theta[["delta_lrt"]] * dest$is_lrt
}
demand <- origins$home_m2 +
  (if ("log_w_floor" %in% names(theta)) exp(theta[["log_w_floor"]]) * origins$work_floor_m2 else 0) +
  (if ("log_w_poi" %in% names(theta)) exp(theta[["log_w_poi"]]) * origins$poi_count else 0)

run_scenario <- function(scenario, uplift = TRUE) {
  dest <- scenario_destinations(scenario, uplift)
  log_dist <- log(dist_mat[, dest$station_id])
  kernel <- exp(-theta[["lambda"]] * log_dist + rep(log_attraction(dest), each = nrow(log_dist)))
  shares <- kernel / rowSums(kernel)
  dest$predicted <- best_fit$kappa * drop(crossprod(shares, demand))
  list(dest = dest, shares = shares)
}

run_existing <- run_scenario("existing")
run_both <- run_scenario("both")
run_no_uplift <- run_scenario("both", uplift = FALSE)

# The re-run must reproduce the report's saved predictions
check <- run_both$dest |>
  select(station_id, predicted) |>
  inner_join(both |> select(station_id, saved = predicted), by = "station_id")
stopifnot(max(abs(check$predicted - check$saved) / check$saved) < 1e-6)
```

## Research question

:::::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
Singapore is building the Jurong Region Line (24 stations) and Cross Island Line Phase 1 (12 stations). Before they open, planners need to know:

- Which new stations will be busy, and which may be quiet?
- Which existing stations will lose riders to them?
- Which neighbourhoods get real walking access to rail?
:::

:::::: {.column width="42%"}
::: stat
[36]{.value}[proposed stations]{.label}
:::

::: stat
[29]{.value}[new places to board]{.label}
:::

::: stat
[7]{.value}[existing stations that gain a line]{.label}
:::
::::::
::::::::

```{r}
#| label: network-map

network_points <- bind_rows(
  stations |>
    filter(in_baseline) |>
    transmute(group = "Existing station"),
  proposed |>
    transmute(
      group = case_when(

        line == "JRL" ~ "New: Jurong Region Line",
        TRUE ~ "New: Cross Island Line Ph 1"
      )
    )
) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Existing station", "New: Jurong Region Line", "New: Cross Island Line Ph 1", "Gains a new line"))) |>
  arrange(group)

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = planning_areas, fill = land, color = "#d9d8d0", linewidth = 0.2) +

  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +

  theme_void(base_size = 15) +
```

### Homes vs workplaces

```{r}
#| label: demand-mix
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 4.3
demand_mix <- bind_rows(
  homes |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(planning_area) |>
    summarise(value = sum(home_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(measure = "Residential footprint"),
  workplaces |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    group_by(planning_area) |>
    summarise(value = sum(work_floor_m2), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(measure = "Workplace floor area")
) |>
  filter(!is.na(planning_area)) |>
  group_by(measure) |>
  mutate(share = value / sum(value)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  complete(planning_area, measure, fill = list(value = 0, share = 0))

top_demand_areas <- demand_mix |>
  group_by(planning_area) |>
  summarise(largest_share = max(share), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(largest_share, n = 12) |>
  pull(planning_area)

demand_order <- demand_mix |>
  filter(planning_area %in% top_demand_areas, measure == "Residential footprint") |>
  arrange(share) |>
  pull(planning_area)

demand_mix |>
  filter(planning_area %in% top_demand_areas) |>
  mutate(planning_area = factor(planning_area, levels = demand_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = share, y = planning_area)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = planning_area), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(color = measure), size = 3.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Residential footprint" = blue, "Workplace floor area" = orange)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(x = "Share of Singapore total", y = NULL) +
  theme_es(15) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

## Analytical approach

::: kicker
A Huff model: riders at each place choose among stations by distance and attractiveness.
:::

::::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[1. Where trips start]{.card-title}

- `r fmt_num(nrow(home_access))` HDB buildings, weighted by footprint
- Workplace and activity locations in 500 m cells
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[2. What makes a station attractive]{.card-title}

- Number of lines
- MRT versus LRT-only
- Bus stops within 400, 500 or 800 m, roughly 5- and 10-minute walks. The best-fitting radius is kept.
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[3. Calibrate, test, apply]{.card-title}

- Fit distance decay and attraction to observed entries
- Test on five geographic groups of stations the model has not seen
- Apply to four networks: today, +JRL, +CRL, both
:::
::::
:::::::::

::: {.small .muted}
The model shares today's trips out among stations. It does not add riders from future housing or from people switching from buses and cars.
:::

## How well the model works

### Error by model

```{r}
#| label: model-ladder
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 4.1
model_wape |>
  mutate(label = factor(model_labels[model], levels = rev(model_labels))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(in_sample, cv_wape), names_to = "measure", values_to = "wape") |>
  mutate(measure = if_else(measure == "cv_wape", "Unseen stations", "Fitted stations")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = wape, y = label)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = label), color = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(aes(color = measure), size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Fitted stations" = "#86b6ef", "Unseen stations" = "#1c5cab")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Weighted absolute percentage error (lower is better)", y = NULL) +
  theme_es(16) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: error-by-type
```

### Stability

```{r}
#| label: fold-stability
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 4.1
parameter_labels <- c(
  lambda = "Distance decay",
  gamma_lines = "Rail lines",
  gamma_bus = "Bus stops",
  delta_lrt = "LRT-only",
  log_w_floor = "Workplace weight",
  log_w_poi = "Activity weight"
)

model_fits$fold_parameters |>
  filter(model == best_model) |>
  mutate(parameter = factor(parameter_labels[parameter], levels = parameter_labels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = 0)) +
  geom_point(color = "#86b6ef", size = 3) +
  geom_point(
    data = tibble(parameter = factor(parameter_labels[names(theta)], levels = parameter_labels), value = unname(theta)),
    shape = "|", size = 9, color = "#0d366b"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = breaks_pretty(n = 3)) +
  labs(x = "Estimate (bar: all stations; points: each test fold)", y = NULL) +
  theme_es(13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "#e1e0d9"),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(1.2, "lines")
  )
```

### Distance decay


### By line

```{r}
#| label: line-impact
#| fig-width: 7.6
#| fig-height: 4.3
line_of <- function(code) {
  prefix <- str_extract(code, "^[A-Z]+")
  merged <- c(CG = "EW", CE = "CC", BP = "BPLRT", SE = "SLRT", SW = "SLRT", STC = "SLRT", PE = "PLRT", PW = "PLRT", PTC = "PLRT")
  coalesce(unname(merged[prefix]), prefix)
}
line_names <- c(
  NS = "North-South", EW = "East-West", NE = "North East", CC = "Circle", DT = "Downtown",
  TE = "Thomson-East Coast", BPLRT = "Bukit Panjang LRT", SLRT = "Sengkang LRT", PLRT = "Punggol LRT"
)

line_impact <- station_change |>
  inner_join(
    code_lookup |>
      mutate(line = line_of(code)) |>
      distinct(station_id, line) |>
      group_by(station_id) |>
      mutate(weight = 1 / n()) |>
      ungroup(),
    by = "station_id",
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  group_by(line) |>
  summarise(net_change = sum(change * weight), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(line_name = fct_reorder(line_names[line], net_change, .desc = TRUE))

ggplot(line_impact, aes(x = net_change, y = line_name)) +
  geom_col(fill = if_else(line_impact$net_change < 0, red, blue), width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = ink_secondary, linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_comma()) +
  labs(x = "Net change in predicted weekday entries", y = NULL) +
  theme_es() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
```

### Catchment map

```{r}
#| label: catchment-map
home_rows <- origins$origin_type == "home"
preferred_station <- function(run) {
  by_subzone <- rowsum(run$shares[home_rows, ] * origins$home_m2[home_rows], origins$subzone_id[home_rows])
  tibble(subzone_id = rownames(by_subzone), station_id = colnames(run$shares)[max.col(by_subzone, ties.method = "first")])
}

catchment_map <- preferred_station(run_existing) |>
  rename(before = station_id) |>
  inner_join(preferred_station(run_both) |> rename(after = station_id), by = "subzone_id") |>
  mutate(changed = before != after) |>
  inner_join(x = subzones, by = "subzone_id") |>
  st_transform(4326)

leaflet(catchment_map, width = "100%", height = 400) |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = if_else(catchment_map$changed, blue, "#d9d8d0"),
    fillOpacity = 0.7,
    color = "white",
    weight = 0.6,
    label = str_c(catchment_map$subzone, ": ", label_of[catchment_map$before], " → ", label_of[catchment_map$after])
  ) |>
  addLegend(colors = c(blue, "#d9d8d0"), labels = c("Preferred station changes", "No change"), position = "bottomright")
```

:::: {.column width="36%"}
::: small
- The biggest losses are at `r str_c(losers$label, collapse = ", ")`. Most losing stations sit on the western East–West Line, next to the JRL.
- Stations that gain a CRL platform gain the most, led by Hougang (+`r fmt_pct(hougang$change_pct, 0)`).
- The Interchange uplift tab shows how much of that gain rests on one assumption: that an extra line attracts riders.
- The Catchment map shows which subzones switch their preferred station. Hover over a subzone for details.

## Public-safety implications

::::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[Crowding at new interchanges]{.card-title}

Hougang's predicted weekday entries rise from `r fmt_num(hougang$existing, -2)` to `r fmt_num(hougang$both, -2)`. At today's peak share, its busiest hour (`r sprintf("%02d:00", hougang_peak$peak_hour)`) would see about `r fmt_num(hougang$both * hougang_peak$peak_share, -2)` entries, before counting riders changing lines. Platform and concourse capacity should be checked against this.
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[Quiet stations]{.card-title}

`r str_c(quiet_new$station_label, collapse = " and ")` are predicted to see few riders. Low footfall means fewer people around at off-peak hours, so lighting, CCTV coverage and staffing need attention from the start.
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="33%"}
::: card
[Walking access and disruption]{.card-title}

Estates that remain beyond 800 m, such as `r str_c(far_after$subzone[1:2], collapse = " and ")`, rely on long walks or feeder buses. Safe crossings on walking routes, and bus bridging plans for rail disruptions, matter most there.
:::
::::
:::::::::

## Limitations

- The total number of trips is fixed. The model moves today's trips between stations, so it cannot add riders from new housing such as Tengah, or from people leaving buses and cars.
- Distances are straight lines. Real walks are longer, and expressways, rivers and fences can make a nearby station hard to reach.
- Homes are weighted by HDB building footprint, not by residents, and workplaces come from OpenStreetMap, whose coverage varies.
- Only entries are modelled. Transfers inside the network are not, so crowding at interchanges is understated.
- With no age data, effects on older residents could not be tested.
- City-centre stations are under-predicted, because many of their riders come from outside the modelled demand.

## Recommendations

1.  Gather local evidence on future housing and jobs for the quiet stations (`r str_c(quiet_new$station_label, collapse = ", ")`) before fixing service levels and opening dates.
2.  Review feeder buses around the stations that lose riders (`r str_c(losers$label, collapse = ", ")`), so routes follow riders to the new lines.
3.  Check capacity and safety at the new interchanges, starting with Hougang, using transfer counts as well as entries.
4.  Improve walking routes and feeder links for estates that stay beyond 800 m of a station, such as `r str_c(far_after$subzone, collapse = ", ")`.

::: {.small .muted}
Full method, data checks and code: [technical report](Take-home_Ex03.html).
:::
